title: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On the eternity of God; definition
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On the eternity of God.

There follows GOD's sixth attribute, namely eternity, which is His highest perfection, by which He is free from finite duration. The word eternity properly notes a standing duration without beginning, middle, end, without flux of past, present, future.
Among the ancients Boethius defines thus: Eternity is the whole, simultaneous, and perfect possession of interminable life — or it is interminable, indivisible, and independent duration.

title: Eternity vs time; essential vs participated; Albertus Magnus
english: It differs from time, as Clement of Alexandria is authority. Improperly it is attributed both to things which, though they have a beginning of time, will yet have no end — as angels, demons, rational souls — and to those which are long-lasting.

Hence Albert the Great: Eternal is said in two ways, namely by essence and by participation. By essence God alone is eternal. But by participation that is said to be eternal which participates some property of eternity — immutability and lack of end — analogically, not univocally.

title: Proofs 1-7 that God is properly eternal
english: I demonstrate that God is properly eternal — that is, without beginning or end, never about to cease. FIRST, from the testimony of sacred Scripture: Psalm 90:2; Isaiah 57:16; Genesis 21:33; Daniel 7:13; Romans 16:26; 1 Timothy 1:17. SECOND, from the immutability of essence. THIRD, from the absolute necessity of existing. FOURTH, from independence.

FIFTH, from simplicity of nature. SIXTH, from catholic consent — Athenagoras, Cyprian, Augustine, Gregory, Anselm, Bernard, Albert the Great. SEVENTH, from the reckoning of the philosophers — Aristotle, Metaphysics XII.7.

title: Against Vorstius on eternity; rules 1-3
english: Conrad Vorstius contradicts this doctrine in Notes on Disputation III On God p. 226, contending that the common opinion of eternity existing all at once is false. For that reason we hand down certain foundations and rules here.

1. God's eternity is not an accident, but God's substance — for it is in reality nothing other than God's duration, and duration nothing other than persevering existence. 2. God's eternity is indivisible and entirely simultaneous, and has no parts succeeding one another. 3. God's eternity, being indivisible, necessarily exists with all differences of times — not that all parts of time exist together among themselves, but that each part of time, while it is in act, exists with eternity.

title: Rules 4-8; pastoral close — Cap. 13 COMPLETE
english: 4. God acts in time not by being subject to time, but by subjecting a finite thing to time. 5. In God there is prior and posterior not by reason of essence or time, but by reason of order among the persons of the Holy Trinity and among His attributes, by reason of our intellect. God's inward works are an act always lasting; but outward works are finished according to God's free will.

6. All things are present to God not by reason of existence, but of knowledge. 7. Eternal years and days of eternity are not said of God because of a division of eternity in itself, but because of the division of perpetuity and time, which He contains under Himself excellently. 8. We ought to imitate God's eternity by constant activity of the good, by unceasing desire of blessed eternity. For that reason I seal the chapter on God's eternity with this monition: THINK ON ETERNITY.
